newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT-Reader's Digest still neutral.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Reader's Digest still neutral.

text.p: Alex. Brown analyst Peter Appert said late Thursday he was maintaining a neutral rating on Reader's Digest Association Inc, citing "no evidence of a turnaround in the fundamentals."
-- company reported fourth quarter loss of $0.22 per share versus profit $0.42.
-- Appert said the results were "not a surprise," as the company had warned Wall Street about fourth charges of $64 million and a quarterly loss.
-- said the 1997 earnings of $1.24 were slightly above his estimate of $1.20.
-- said he would wait to see how interim chief executive George Grune spent the $400 million set aside to boost its businesses, and whether he will spend more or less.
-- said the "near-term earnings outlook is very cloudy for this company, and I expect that earnings will remain under pressure all the way through 1998."
-- cited falling unit sales in all of its various book business, including condensed books, in 1997 compared to 1996. Books are the largest part of the revenue pie for the direct-mail division.
